use_cases.attribution: Zendesk ticket status · 48hr recontact rate · Payment-gateway chargeback flag · Post-resolution CSAT

use_cases.name: Skip / Cancel Flow

use_cases.name: Retention Save

pilot.name: Billing / Skip / Credit Automation
pilot.description: Rules-based, non-retention, non-escalation — the single lowest-risk, highest-ROI category in the entire Fabletics contact mix. Directly addresses the #1 pain point surfaced by Julie's team: "members not understanding skip deadlines" and "feeling tricked by VIP membership."
why_first: 35% of all contacts (~1.65M/yr) — single largest driver
Rules-based decision trees (skip Y/N, credit lookup, charge explanation) — no policy judgment
Knowledge base documented in Helpjuice (skip deadline, $59.95 charge, credits)
what_we_stand_up: AI voice + chat agent on Genesys — English & Spanish
Proactive skip-deadline reminder outbound — 48 hrs before the 5th
Warm transfer to Startek agents with full context — no re-explaining
Real-time containment, AHT, CSAT dashboard for ops
Zendesk / Helpjuice / Medallia integrations wired in
what_client_does: 15–23 hours total over 6–8 weeks — split across Julie, Dan, and one IT contact
No dedicated FTE, no new hires, no IT buildout — we plug into Genesys, CRM, Helpjuice, Zendesk
Anyreach + Startek absorb 95%+ of implementation effort
One named IT POC to unblock API / system access
commercial_offer: One vendor, one price — replaces Cognigy + a portion of current BPO
Priced per resolved member outcome — not per hour or per token
Resolution = query addressed with no repeat contact within 48 hrs
Ramp risk on us — containment misses hit our margin, not your invoice
Joint validation period defined in SOW before volumes scale
pilot.phase2_unlocks: Shipping / WISMO · Retention Save · Training needs analysis automation · 100% AI-assisted QA

internal_briefing.overview_intro: Robert requested an executive-level ROI model comparing Fabletics' current state (Cognigy + incumbent BPO) against our outcomes-based AI + Human approach. This version integrates the Fabletics Q&A response (Julie Barton, Dec 5, 2025) — most notably the 22.5% containment rate replacing our earlier 35% industry benchmark, plus FTE rate stepping per Sid's flag and Rafay's commercial review.
internal_briefing.confidentiality_note: Jam disclosed that Fabletics spends approximately $3M on AI annually but explicitly asked that this number not be referenced or shared internally. Our model derives the estimate independently from public Cognigy pricing data applied to Fabletics-stated volumes. Never cite Jam as a source. Always say "industry benchmark" or "back-of-envelope from public billing model." The external brief includes an asterisk footnote spelling out the derivation so the ~$2.9M appears as our work product, not leaked intel.

lead_with: $3.00/outcome is already 35% below their current $4.62 blended cost. No ramp period where they're paying more.
Price steps down as AI containment improves. Floor-protected — pricing never steps up if milestones aren't jointly verified.
They pay per resolved outcome. If we don't resolve it, they don't pay. We absorb the ramp risk.
Replaces Cognigy + incumbent BPO with a single outcomes-based partner. One SLA, one invoice.
if_pushed_on_price: Their Cognigy alone costs $2.74 per AI-resolved contact
— and it only handles 22.5% of volume. Our $3.00 includes AI + human for 100% of contacts.
Their BPO costs $5.17 per human-resolved contact.
Our blended $3.00 is below that even before AI efficiencies kick in.
The $4.62 blended CPI is before any revenue generation.
Our platform also drives $38M+ in new revenue opportunities they can't access today (Phase 2+).

If They Ask About the Cognigy Spend Esti: We derived it from Cognigy's public billing model
(per-conversation pricing) applied to Fabletics' stated contact volumes. Back-of-envelope benchmark. Published in the brief with an asterisk footnote spelling out the math.
Never say: "Jam told us it was $3M."
Always say: "Industry benchmarks suggest..." or "Our estimate based on public pricing data."
If They Ask About the 22.5% Containment: Sourced directly from your own Q&A response to us (Julie, Dec 5, 2025).
"Roughly 20–25% of inquiries are handled by self-service or chatbot tools." We used the 22.5% midpoint. Defensible, client-validated, non-controversial.
If They Ask About Revenue Generation: Frame as cherry on top, not the core value.
The cost story stands on its own. Revenue generation is upside.

Julie's Q&A was explicit that proactive outreach and cross-sell/upsell are outside the scope of Global Member Services. Position these as Phase 2+ opportunities requiring engagement beyond the core GMS contract — not as Day 1 contractual savings.

red_lines: Never reference the $3M AI spend as a sourced number from Jam. Our published figure is ~$2.9M derived independently from public pricing.
Never share our internal margins or cost structure with Fabletics.
Never share per-minute Anyreach rates or Startek hourly rates.
Never position this as "replacing" Cognigy — frame as "elevating" their CX with a blended model.
Never guarantee specific revenue generation numbers — always "potential" or "opportunity." Revenue gen now has an explicit scope caveat in the brief.
Never commit to containment percentages as guarantees — pricing is floor-protected but milestones require joint validation, not contractual guarantees.
Never promise a 4-week go-live — the brief says 6–8 weeks to align with Fabletics' own stated 4–6 month evaluation window.
next_steps: Robert reviews v3 brief and updated xlsx model (numbers reconciled; 22.5% containment sourced).
Rafay legal/commercial review — stress-test liability language, especially the floor-protection language and "joint validation period" phrasing.

FTE rate stepping (NEW in v5): rates now step up across phases ($10 → $11 → $12) per Sid's flag and Rafay's commercial review request. Margin profile reflects honest blended cost (FTE labor + AI platform). Phase 1 margin is thin — we cannot concede further on Phase 1 price.
Share the client-facing brief (separate doc) with Tom Lynch, Julie Barton, and Dan Brady.

Upon client interest, prepare SOW for the 6–8 wk billing/skip/credit lighthouse pilot.
